name: Guard Pass from Chill Dog
description: Passing Chill Dog requires clearing the isolated arm and high-leg posture control first. Side control also requires a separate clearance of the hips and legs.
summary: Passing Chill Dog first requires clearing the isolated arm and high-leg posture control, then separately clearing the remaining guard.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Chill Dog; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. A high-guard escape and a completed pass are separate checkpoints. Side control requires the hips and legs to be clear as well as the head.

Keep the free hand available for framing while preventing the isolated elbow from being pulled further away from your torso. The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (top): What needs freeing before you begin the pass?
flashcards.answer: Clear the upper-body leg-and-arm enclosure before committing to a separate pass around the remaining knees.
flashcards.answer_line: Neck and shoulder from high guard

plausible: Only hand; elbow remains outside
Only the free leg against your hip
trap: Only head; knee hug still traps arm

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (top): What does their arm moving around your head indicate?
flashcards.answer: The head-side grip change advances New York toward Chill Dog; it is an upper-body guard-control cue.
flashcards.answer_line: Neck clears; their arm trap remains

plausible: Knee hug opens to release your arm
Wrist pummel begins under your hand
trap: Second leg closes the high clinch

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (top): How should the free arm help before clearance?
flashcards.answer: Early inside framing helps preserve space while the isolated arm is released; pressure is not a substitute for clearance.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside frame with a balanced base

plausible: Reach over back; yield inside space
Post far away; caught elbow flares

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (top): Where should you make space to loosen the high leg?
flashcards.answer: Create slack at the high-leg connection with balanced positioning before extracting the head or shoulder.
flashcards.answer_line: At hip and thigh, with head aligned

plausible: At fingers; thigh remains clamped
At free ankle; high thigh tight
trap: At knee base; head-thigh stay linked

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (top): When can the shoulder leave the leg enclosure?
flashcards.answer: Withdraw shoulder and elbow through slack in the high leg rather than pulling an isolated arm through resistance.
flashcards.answer_line: High leg opens; shoulder moves free

plausible: Free hand first touches their hip
Knees clear; shoulder remains held

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (top): What confirms a completed side-control pass?
flashcards.answer: Side control requires clearing the legs and hips and establishing a stable pin beside the torso after the high enclosure releases.
flashcards.answer_line: Legs clear; chest pins beside torso

plausible: Head free; both knees between you
Shoulder free; one leg still trapped
trap: Chest by ribs; ankle still trapped

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (top): The head is free but a knee blocks your hip; what remains?
flashcards.answer: Head clearance completes only the first escape checkpoint. The blocking knee must also be passed before side control exists.
flashcards.answer_line: Pass the remaining knee, then settle

plausible: Call the low chest contact a pass
Step past foot; leave knee inside

defender.name: Guard Pass from Chill Dog Defender
defender.description: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (defender): Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Chill Dog; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. A high-guard escape and a completed pass are separate checkpoints. Side control requires the hips and legs to be clear as well as the head.

Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee. Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.

Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist. Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup. Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Release the failing high connection and make a short hip escape behind a shoulder frame before the passer settles. Guard retention depends on returning a knee to that space, not on keeping an unloaded leg hanging behind the head.
key_principles: Secure New York first: Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip.
Turn onto the hip: Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee.
Clear the neck: Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.
Place the inside frame: Use the forearm near the shoulder line to manage forward pressure; do not let the frame collapse across your own wrist.
Maintain the arm trap: Keep the knee hug while choosing further control such as Invisible Collar or an omoplata setup.
Recover when control opens: Return the legs to a comfortable guard if the opponent withdraws the elbow or stacks your upper back.

The opponent changing the hand around your head signals the move beyond New York, not a turtle escape.
Create slack at the hip and thigh while keeping the head and captured arm aligned.

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (bottom): What preserves the existing trap during their first escape?
flashcards.answer: Retain the New York arm isolation and knee support while they seek slack, provided the position remains comfortable.
flashcards.answer_line: Their arm outside; your knee hugged

plausible: Let elbow inside while pulling head
Let knee go; rely on foot grip alone
trap: Keep knee high; let overhook open

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (bottom): How should you adjust if your high knee drifts away?
flashcards.answer: A hip-angle correction brings the knee toward the torso and supports the high leg without dragging the foot.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip turn brings braced knee forward

plausible: Pull ankle back with hip still flat
Straighten leg over their shoulder
trap: Lift foot higher; leave knee behind

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (bottom): Their shoulder approaches as Chill Dog opens; where frame?
flashcards.answer: An inside forearm protects space while the hip moves and the knee returns, reducing the passer's crossface access.

plausible: Behind shoulder with elbow away
Over head with both hands clasped

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (bottom): What follows when the isolated elbow has escaped?
flashcards.answer: Once the elbow and high connection fail, prioritize guard retention behind a shoulder frame rather than reaching for the lost grip.
flashcards.answer_line: Open loose high leg; bring knee in

plausible: Leave loose leg behind their head
Both hands chase the escaped wrist
trap: Both hands regrip ankle before knee

flashcards.question: Guard Pass from Chill Dog (bottom): What prevents their head clearance becoming a pass?
flashcards.answer: The passer still has to clear your knees and hips; maintain the inside barrier as the upper-body control opens.

plausible: Hand grip only, both knees outside
High foot without knee support
trap: Forearm in; near knee outside hip
